scenes.headline: Union
scenes.subtitle: Stacking two DataFrames row-wise.
scenes.narration: A union stacks two DataFrames on top of each other, combining their rows into one DataFrame.

scenes.headline: Union essentials
items: union combines rows by column position
unionByName matches columns by name instead
Schemas must be compatible on both sides
It keeps duplicates unless you call distinct
scenes.narration: Union combines rows by column position, while unionByName matches columns by their names. The schemas on both sides must be compatible, and union keeps duplicate rows unless you follow it with distinct.

scenes.headline: Union by name is safer
scenes.code:
combined = jan_sales.unionByName(feb_sales)

# Remove duplicates if needed
unique = combined.distinct()
scenes.narration: We combine January and February sales with unionByName, which aligns columns by name so a different column order cannot silently misalign the data. If duplicates are possible, we follow up with distinct to remove them.

scenes.text: Prefer unionByName over union so column order differences never corrupt your data.
scenes.narration: Prefer unionByName over plain union so that any difference in column order can never quietly corrupt your combined data.
